title: Detecting Institutional Hypocrisy: An X–Y–Z Coherence Test
description:
This paper applies the Coherence Constraint Instrument (X–Y–Z) to detect institutional hypocrisy using publicly documented evidence only.
Institutional hypocrisy is operationally defined as persistent inconsistency between declared commitments (X), observable actions (Y), and realized outcomes (Z). No intent inference, moral judgment, or belief framework is used.
Procedure
Identify one commitment (X), one subsequent action (Y), and one resulting outcome (Z).
Record a coherence violation if any of the following occur:
the action contradicts the commitment
the outcome contradicts the action
the outcome contradicts the commitment
Hypocrisy is recorded only if violations recur or appear across multiple constraint pairs. Single, isolated events are insufficient.
Output
Violation detected / not detected
Constraint pairs violated
Persistence present / absent
Optional numeric projection may be included as a derived summary only.
Boundary Conditions
Missing or ambiguous evidence yields no conclusion. Local violations do not imply global system failure.
Status
Applied diagnostic execution. Instrument-consistent. Non-conceptual.
